clues.q: Domesticated from the red junglefowl about 8,000 years ago, this is one of the most widespread domestic animals, raised for meat and eggs
These mostly nocturnal birds of prey have large, broad heads, binocular vision and feathers adapted for silent flight
These flightless sea birds with flippers live almost exclusively in the Southern Hemisphere
Native to Africa, this flightless bird is the largest living species of bird
These mostly tropical birds have a strong curved beak and clawed feet; one-third of their species are threatened with extinction
Found worldwide except Australia, New Zealand, Madagascar and the polar regions, these forest birds of the family Picidae include sapsuckers
These large, heavyset birds of the Americas have a fleshy wattle called a snood hanging from the base of the bill
These large water birds have a long beak and a big throat pouch used for catching prey and draining water before swallowing
Also called the wild duck, this dabbling duck breeds throughout North America, Eurasia and North Africa
These wading birds of the family Phoenicopteridae include four species in the Americas and two in Afro-Eurasia
This sea eagle and bird of prey found near large bodies of water in North America forms a species pair with the white-tailed eagle
These birds native to the Americas form the family Trochilidae, with around 375 species from Alaska to Tierra del Fuego
Males of this South Asian bird are called peacocks and females peahens, though both are often colloquially called peacocks
These brightly marked Neotropical birds of the family Ramphastidae have large, often colorful bills
This extinct flightless bird was endemic to Mauritius; its closest living relative is the Nicobar pigeon
This wild member of the family Columbidae is the ancestor of the domesticated pigeons familiar to most people
About the size of a chicken, these flightless birds endemic to New Zealand are the smallest ratites
Also called the red cardinal, this bird of the genus Cardinalis is found through the eastern United States south to Guatemala
Endemic to Australia, this flightless bird is the continent's tallest native bird and the third-tallest living bird
Also known as the polar owl, this large Arctic owl is the only owl with mainly white plumage
These large, long-legged, long-necked wading birds with long, stout bills make up the family Ciconiidae
These long-legged, long-necked birds of the family Ardeidae include species called egrets and bitterns
The largest waterfowl, these birds of the genus Cygnus are closely related to geese and ducks
This large all-black bird is the most widely distributed corvid and the heaviest passerine
This migratory thrush, widespread throughout North America, was named after a European bird because of its reddish-orange breast
This long-legged member of the cuckoo family from the southwestern U.S. and Mexico is also called the chaparral cock
Also called the common puffin, this seabird of the auk family breeds from Russia and Iceland to as far south as Maine
This large kingfisher with a brown eye-stripe has a distinctive call, often given by several birds at once, used as a stock jungle sound effect
These medium-sized owls of the genus Tyto have characteristic heart-shaped faces
This crow-sized bird of prey known for its speed has a blue-gray back and a black head; in North America it was once called the "duck hawk"
This large goose has a black head and neck, white cheeks and a brown body; it is native to North America
Also known as the common parakeet or budgie, this small, long-tailed, seed-eating parrot is naturally green and yellow
These 22 parrot species of the family Cacatuidae are native to Australasia
These large seabirds of the family Diomedeidae are found mostly in the Southern Ocean and North Pacific but are absent from the North Atlantic
These large, long-tailed, often colorful New World parrots are popular as companion birds
This crested member of the crow family native to eastern North America has a white chest and a black U-shaped collar
Historically called the sea hawk or fish hawk, this large fish-eating raptor is brown above and grayish on the head and underparts
The most widely distributed species of eagle, this dark brown raptor is one of the best-known birds of prey in the Northern Hemisphere
These small to medium-sized, brightly colored birds of the family Alcedinidae are often found near calm ponds and small rivers
Endemic to Antarctica, this is the tallest and heaviest of all living penguins, with bright-yellow ear patches
Males of this small bird have black, white and brown markings; humans have introduced it to most parts of the world
With a wingspan up to 3.3 meters, this New World vulture of western South America is one of the largest flying birds
Extinct in the wild in 1987 but since reintroduced, this New World vulture is the largest North American land bird
These flightless ratites live in the tropical forests of New Guinea, the Moluccas and northeastern Australia
Also called the tiger owl or hoot owl, this is the most widely distributed true owl in North America and a regular predator of skunks

clues.q: The pink color of this social wading bird of the ibis family comes from its diet, like the American flamingo's
This large, mostly ground-dwelling bird of prey is endemic to the grasslands and savannas of sub-Saharan Africa
These birds of Africa, Asia and Melanesia have a long, down-curved bill that sometimes bears a horny casque
Native to the eastern Pacific, males of this marine bird show off their brightly colored feet by lifting them while strutting before a female
This strongly migratory bird sees two summers each year, flying from northern breeding grounds to the Antarctic coast and back
This small nonmigratory North American bird of the tit family, with white cheeks and a dark bib, is well known for its vocalizations
One of the most common hawks in North America, this raptor is one of three U.S. species colloquially called the "chickenhawk"
These ground-dwelling Australian birds are famous for mimicking natural and artificial sounds and for the male's huge, fanned tail
This extinct North American bird's name comes from the French for "passing by," due to its migratory habits
Also called the whale-headed stork, this large African wading bird is named for its enormous, shoe-shaped bill
This large neotropical eagle of lowland rainforests is the largest bird of prey throughout its range
Its name means "ancient wing"; this feathered, bird-like dinosaur was long accepted as the oldest known bird
The most widespread New World vulture, this bird ranges from southern Canada to the southern tip of South America
This small Old World bird is known for its powerful song, often described as one of the most beautiful sounds in nature
The most widespread swallow in the world, this bird has blue upperparts and a long, deeply forked tail
This cinnamon-colored bird has black and white wings, a tall erectile crest, a long downcurved bill, and a soft "oop-oop-oop" call
Called "redbreast" in the British Isles, this small insect-eating bird of the Old World flycatcher family is found across Europe
Commonly found in North America and also in parts of the Caribbean and Hawaii, this songbird belongs to the family Mimidae
This large wading bird is common near shores across North and Central America; an all-white population lives in South Florida
clues.a: What is the great blue heron?

clues.q: Also called the rain dove and once the Carolina pigeon, this is one of the most abundant North American birds and a popular gamebird
This large crane of North America and northeastern Siberia uses Nebraska's central Platte River Valley as its most important stopover area
Also called the great northern diver, breeding adults of this water bird have a black head and neck with a greenish or purplish sheen
Sometimes called the owl-parrot, this large, nocturnal, ground-dwelling parrot is endemic to New Zealand
Found mainly in New Guinea, these passerines of the family Paradisaeidae are best known for the long, elaborate plumes of the males
This bird of the trogon family lives in the cloud forests of Central America and southern Mexico and mainly eats fruits of the laurel family
Named for its calls, this endangered crane is the tallest North American bird; only 21 remained in the wild in 1941
This large, olive-green parrot with brilliant orange under its wings lives in the alpine regions of New Zealand's South Island
Native to East Asia, this elaborately colored perching duck is closely related to the North American wood duck
Driven extinct in the mid-1800s, this flightless alcid gave its old name to the Southern Hemisphere birds that resembled it
The largest of these extinct flightless birds of New Zealand stood about 12 feet tall with necks outstretched
These extinct flightless birds of Madagascar laid the largest eggs known for any amniote
This small, long-legged owl of the open Americas nests in underground tunnels, usually ones dug by other animals
Also called the man o' war, this seabird with a wingspan up to 2.4 meters is the largest of its family
This medium-sized passerine has glossy black plumage with a metallic sheen, speckled with white at some times of year; its bill is yellow in summer
This small seed-eating bird of the cardinal family often migrates by night, using the stars to navigate
This true thrush breeds in Europe, western Asia and North Africa and has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand
This small ground-nesting game bird of the pheasant family breeds in the Palearctic and winters in Africa and southern India
This black-and-white member of the crow family is a resident breeding bird across northern Europe and Asia
This tropical bird of Amazon and Orinoco swamps is the only living species in its order, and its relationships are still debated
Also known as the lammergeier, this large bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet is 70 to 90 percent bone
Also called the snakebird, this water bird of the Americas swims with only its neck above water, looking like a snake ready to strike
This small migratory North American thrush lives in open woodlands, farmlands and orchards
Some wing feathers of this brown, gray and yellow North American bird have red tips resembling sealing wax
This large plover of the Americas has two black bands across its breast and a shrill, two-syllable call that gives it its name
Males of these birds of the family Ptilonorhynchidae build a structure decorated with sticks and brightly colored objects to attract a mate
The genus name of these two African bird species, Buphagus, means "ox eater" in Greek
Also called indicator birds, these mostly African birds are best known for their interaction with humans
Once called the "rice bird," this small New World blackbird breeds in the northern U.S. and Canada and winters in southern South America
Typically the heaviest eagle in the world, this dark brown Pacific raptor has white wings and tail and a yellow beak
About the size of a sparrow, this tiny owl of the Southwest often nests in woodpecker holes in saguaro cacti
The largest flying bird native to Africa, the male of this species may be the heaviest living animal capable of flight
Sometimes called the "undertaker bird" for its cloak-like wings, this large African stork often breeds near landfills
Also called the rose-breasted cockatoo, this pink and gray bird is one of Australia's most abundant species
Common along Australia's eastern seaboard from northern Queensland to South Australia, this parrot lives in rainforest, coastal bush and woodland
These coastal waders of the family Haematopodidae, found worldwide except polar regions, all belong to the single genus Haematopus
